solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unit of land held by nameless Greek poet

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside it, so the unit of land goes within the word for nameless

parts.note: anon, short for anonymous, means nameless
an acre is a unit of land area

explanation.surface: A plot of land owned by an unnamed poet in ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Anacreon was a lyric poet of ancient Greece, famous for drinking songs.

clue.text: Backing engineers against sort of laser

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: a sort of laser is the word laser loosely reworked, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Engineers backing a project to build some kind of laser.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal is a going backwards, as backing is a moving in the opposite direction.

clue.text: Court guide's piece that includes editor and bishop

indicators.note: a piece that includes others holds them within itself, so editor and bishop go inside

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A guide to the royal court has a section covering an editor and a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' and 'bishop' both belong to chess, though the surface is about the court and the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Book was a directory of people at court and in the government, a peerage-style register.

clue.text: Dickens character after old penny for tedious task

indicators.note: the Dickens character comes after the old penny, so it follows in the answer

parts.note: D stood for the penny in British money before 1971
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: Reading Dickens for an old penny sounds like a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudge, like drudgery, can name dull, laborious work as well as the person doing it.

clue.text: Disclose university five seized by backward property right

indicators.note: a thing seized by another is gripped inside it, so five goes inside the property right
the property right word is read from end to start

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep another's property until a debt is paid
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Revealing that a university's five were taken by a creditor exercising a claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns LIEN into NEIL, and 'seized by' puts V inside it to make NVEIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To unveil is to reveal, take the cover off, synonym of disclose.

clue.text: Mass producers maybe trick star with pompous speeches

parts.note: to con is to trick or swindle
a celeb, short for celebrity, is a star
rants are loud, bombastic speeches

explanation.surface: Factory mass production depends on a con, a celebrity and some ranting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass producers' suggests industry; it means priests who say Mass together.
explanation.definitionFit: Concelebrants are priests jointly celebrating the Eucharist, so they produce a Mass together.

clue.text: Crack sovereign measure to bear down on East European plant

indicators.note: in a down entry the measure sits on top of, pressing down on, the letters below it

parts.note: a chink is a narrow crack
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword sovereign
an inch is a measure of length
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A cracked coin is measured before pressing down on an Eastern European plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' looks like a gold coin to go with crack, but it gives the monarch ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chincherinchee is a South African bulb plant of the star-of-Bethlehem kind, grown for its white flowers.

clue.text: Vegetables in small utensil, roughly adding nuts

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a pan is a kitchen utensil
the suffix -ish means roughly, approximately
nuts and onions are both slang for heads

explanation.surface: Vegetables put into a small pan, coarsely chopped, with some nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' and 'onion' are both British slang for the head, as in 'off one's onion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish onions are a large, mild variety of onion, a kind of vegetable.

clue.text: Cab provided to return port

indicators.note: returning means the word for provided is written back to front

parts.note: if means provided, as in provided that
Acre is a port in northern Israel

explanation.surface: A taxi agrees to bring someone back to a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiacre is a small four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire, a French hackney cab.

clue.text: Library book I loaned out

indicators.note: out signals the words are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A library book that I have lent out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bodleian is the main research library of the University of Oxford.

clue.text: Letter from island with half missing

indicators.note: losing half of the island's name keeps only its first half

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A letter from an island arrives with half of it lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Those sliding on snow risk crashing around end of the slope without leap

indicators.note: the scrambled risk goes around the final letter of the
crashing suggests the word risk smashed and reassembled
the end of the word the is its last letter
the word slope loses the letters of a word for leap

parts.note: to lope is to move with long bounding leaps

explanation.surface: Skiers take a risk of crashing at the bottom of a slope if they don't jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes the final letter of 'the'; lope, a bounding leap, comes off the front of slope, leaving its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiers glide over snow on skis, which is exactly a description of sliding on it.

clue.text: Veneered dial?

parts.note: dial is the word laid written backwards, so it is laid read over, i.e. reversed

explanation.surface: A clock face with a decorative veneer?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: over is a reversal signal, so LAID reversed gives the clue word DIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlaid means covered with a thin surface layer, as a veneer covers wood.

clue.text: Drunk, lacking limits, produces leak

indicators.note: without its limits the word drunk loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A drunk staggering about until he needs a wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours or liquids that run seep or escape, so to run is to leak.

clue.text: Nude's odd bits left in genuine spin

indicators.note: the odd letters and left go in the word for genuine

parts.note: true means genuine

indicators.note: the odd bits of the word nude are its first and third letters

explanation.surface: A nude figure with odd bits left over taking a real spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits' picks N and D from Nude, and 'in' puts them with L inside TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trundle is to roll or turn along slowly, as a wheel spins.

clue.text: Origins of Darwinism upset orthodox pair

indicators.note: the origins of words are their opening letters, with a nod to Darwin's Origin of Species

explanation.surface: Darwin's ideas upset two orthodox believers.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a set of two, a couple or twosome.

clue.text: Child adopts old approach this evening

indicators.note: a child adopting something takes it in, so the approach goes inside the child

parts.note: a tot is a small child
nigh is an archaic verb meaning to draw near

explanation.surface: A child is taken in by a traditional method this evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight refers to the evening or night of today, the present evening.

clue.text: Badly lost, Del embraces variable dates Julius arranged

indicators.note: the scrambled words embrace, holding within them, the variable
badly suggests the words lost and Del are mangled into a new order

parts.note: Y is a letter conventionally used for an unknown variable in algebra

explanation.surface: Del has made a mess, losing dates on the calendar Julius Caesar set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges LOST DEL into OLDSTLE, and 'embraces' takes in Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Style dating follows the Julian calendar introduced by Julius Caesar, before the Gregorian reform.

clue.text: Confined lion's calm, on speed occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only some letters, here every second one of the words

explanation.surface: A lion is calm, though on drugs now and then, while caged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and so on letters of LIONSCALMONSPEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclosed is an old spelling of enclosed, meaning shut in or confined.

clue.text: Festival band discovered with American disease

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its covering, the outer letters, removed

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A festival band found to have an American illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus, or lockjaw, is a bacterial infection causing muscle spasms.

clue.text: Ben's rose is twisted, short and stiff

indicators.note: twisted words are bent out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ben's rose has bent, its stem cut short and stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: En brosse describes hair cut short and bristly so it stands upright, like a crew cut.

clue.text: Tie-breaker arranged for fun

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A deciding match laid on just for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-off is an extra race or vote held to decide a contest that ended level.

clue.text: Patter disturbed this heartless cook

indicators.note: disturbed means the word this is jumbled into a new order
a heartless word loses its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Chatter has upset this cold-hearted chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' turns THIS into SHTI, and 'heartless' leaves CK from COOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Shtick is a performer's routine, the practised line of chat or gimmick a comic delivers.

clue.text: Move soldier after final month

indicators.note: the soldier comes after the final month in the answer

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the last month
a soldier ant is a worker of a warrior caste in a colony

explanation.surface: A soldier is posted elsewhere after December.
explanation.definitionFit: To decant is to transfer, as wine from bottle to decanter or people rehoused elsewhere.

clue.text: Notes in teachers' paper

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the word notes

explanation.surface: Notes printed in a newspaper for teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times Educational Supplement, a British weekly for teachers, is known by its initials; te is also a sol-fa note, so Notes doubles as a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times Educational Supplement is the weekly newspaper read by UK teachers, known by its initials.

clue.text: Feature polished off, followed by a drink

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
to polish off food is to eat it all

explanation.surface: A face scrubbed clean, followed by a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: China tea is tea grown in China, smoky or delicate, a beverage.

clue.text: Blast soot is unlimited and gushing

parts.note: a toot is a blast on a horn

indicators.note: unlimited means losing the outer limits, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Cursing the soot that is pouring out without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast' is an oath in the surface but a trumpet note in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Too-too means excessively affected or effusive, overdone in sentiment.

clue.text: Energy shown by very loud cute lass excited about north-east success

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
FF, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

indicators.note: the excited letters go about, around, the compass point
excited means the words cute lass are stirred into a new order

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A noisy, lively girl celebrating a win in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges CUTE LASS into ECTUALSS, and 'about' places it around NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Effectualness is the quality of producing the intended result, effectiveness that amounts to success.
